stops.note: 'by weight', from the phrase libra pondo 'a pound by weight'; libra gives the £ sign and the abbreviation lb
borrowed along the Roman frontier; German Pfund and Dutch pond come from the same loan
King Offa of Mercia's coinage reform around 785 struck 240 silver pennies from a pound of silver, the basis of the pound sterling
the 240-penny pound lasted until British decimalisation on 15 February 1971

current_meaning: a unit of weight (about 454 g); the currency of the United Kingdom
